skill: Communicating between the technical and non-technical
expected_level_description: You can: - listen to and interpret the needs of technical and non-technical stakeholders, and manage their expectations - manage active and reactive communication - support or host difficult discussions within the team or with diverse senior stakeholders

You can: - turn complex data into clear and well understood solutions, which can be acted upon - share data communication skills with the team and organisation - understand and communicate different options, taking into account risks and uncertainties
You can: - undertake data profiling and source system analysis - present clear insights to colleagues to support the end use of the data

You can: - ensure data governance supports changes to the organisational strategy - align data governance with wider governance (for example, budget) - assure corporate services by understanding important risks and providing mitigation through assurance mechanisms

You can: - test and evaluate the feasibility of unfamiliar and emerging technologies, or familiar technologies in new data contexts - share what you learn with the organisation, explaining potential benefits, risks, and practical considerations - recommend, design and implement innovative data solutions based on organisation objectives, user needs, and operational constraints

You can: - understand the concepts and principles of data modelling and can produce relevant data models - work across government and industry, recognising opportunities for the reuse and alignment of data models in different organisations - design the method to categorise data models within an organisation

You can: - create data standards for the organisation - advocate for, and oversee compliance with, data policies and standards - decide where standards need to be set across the organisation, and how to set them in the wider context of government

You can: - identify how metadata repositories can support different areas of the organisation - communicate the value of metadata repositories - set up robust governance processes to keep repositories up to date

You can: - anticipate problems and defend against them at the right time - understand how a problem fits into the larger picture - identify and describe problems, and help others to describe them - build problem-solving capabilities in others

You can: - define strategies and policies, providing guidance to others on working in the strategic context - evaluate current strategies to ensure business requirements are being met and exceeded where possible

skill: Turning business problems into data design
expected_level_description: You can: - design data architecture that deals with problems across the enterprise - work across all organisational subject areas and internal and external programmes

You can: - shape organisational strategy using a deep understanding of the health and care system - represent the organisation with health and care partners and leaders - anticipate how policy and service changes will affect digital services and care

You can: - design data models and reference sets using clinical terminologies - map between terminologies and classifications, and explain the limits of a mapping - advise teams on terminology use in products and analytics
You can: - set interoperability standards and strategy for the organisation - lead national or cross-organisation standards work - assure the design of critical integrations across many systems
You can: - set information governance policy and strategy - advise the board on information risk and compliance - represent the organisation with regulators and partners
You can: - define data quality rules and measures - work with data providers to fix the root causes of poor quality

You can: - lead hazard identification and risk assessment for a product or change - write and maintain hazard logs and clinical safety case reports - agree risk controls with product teams and check that they work - advise teams on applying clinical risk management standards
You can: - line manage a team, setting objectives and running appraisals - support wellbeing and manage attendance, performance, and conduct - plan the team's development and succession
